Incorporating the April 2023 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) shifts the tone more cautious than the FOMC statement alone. Banks reported broad-based tightening in standards and terms across C&I and commercial real estate, as well as most consumer categories (credit cards, auto, residential real estate, HELOCs), with wider spreads, higher required DSCRs, and lower LTVs. Reasons cited included a weaker economic outlook, funding costs, deposit outflows, liquidity positions, collateral values, and tighter credit scoring. Loan demand was weaker across business uses (plant/equipment, M&A, inventory, A/R), and banks expected further tightening; foreign and mid-sized banks also tightened, with a minor exception of some easing on GSE-eligible mortgages by mid-sized banks.

Implications: The SLOOS corroborates and amplifies the FOMC’s line that tighter credit conditions will weigh on activity and hiring, suggesting a stronger drag on capex and CRE and a more restrictive transmission to households even without additional rate hikes. While inflation remains elevated, the bank-driven tightening likely substitutes for some policy firming, tilting near-term growth risks to the downside relative to a neutral read.

Net tone: cautious with a modest downside skew to growth relative to the original summary.
